policy_title: Support Small Businesses and Post Offices, and Address Horizon Scandal
stated: Labour will act on late payments for small businesses and the self-employed, improve export guidance, and reform the British Business Bank to better support regional growth. They will also reform procurement rules for government contracts. For the Post Office network, Labour will strengthen it, support new products and services like banking hubs, and ensure swift justice and compensation for sub-postmasters affected by the Horizon IT scandal.

source.quote: Labour’s plan for economic growth has been developed for all UK businesses. But small firms, entrepreneurs, and the selfemployed face unique challenges. That is why, in partnership, Labour has developed a plan for small businesses – the lifeblood of communities and high streets across the country. We will take action on late payments to ensure small businesses and the self-employed are paid on time. We will improve guidance and remove barriers to exporting for small businesses. Reform of the British Business Bank, including a stronger mandate to support growth in the regions and nations, will make it easier for small and medium sized enterprises to access capital. We will also reform procurement rules to give them greater access to government contracts. The Post Office is an essential service in communities across the country. Labour will look for ways to strengthen the Post Office network, in consultation with sub-postmasters, trade unions and customers, and support the development of new products, services and business models, such as banking hubs, that will help reinvigorate the high street. We will also ensure justice and compensation are delivered swiftly for those sub-postmasters shamefully affected by the Horizon IT scandal.

bearing_set.reason: Late payment reform directly affects self-employed and small business owner income security and cash flow; British Business Bank and procurement reforms bear on job quality and viability for small employers.

The Horizon IT scandal element centres on wrongful prosecutions and due process failures — swift justice and compensation for sub-postmasters is a miscarriage-of-justice and rule-of-law matter squarely within O9's scope.

British Business Bank reform for regional growth, improved export guidance, and procurement rule changes all target business investment, economic opportunity, and firm dynamism — the core O13 indicators.

Explicit targeting of regional growth via the British Business Bank reform bears on regional inequality, which is a named O14 indicator; late payment reform also disproportionately benefits smaller firms over large corporates.

membership_note: Four clear bearings: O4 (self-employed income security via late payment reform), O9 (Horizon due-process remedy), O13 (aggregate business opportunity and investment), and O14 (regional inequality via BBB reform). Post Office banking hubs could affect community access but the cohesion mechanism is too indirect to clear the O15 bar.
